stemBlocks.value: A speed–time graph shows an athlete's race: the speed rises steadily from 0 m/s at 0 s to 12 m/s at 6 s, stays at 12 m/s until 10 s, then falls steadily to 0 m/s at 13 s. (i) Determine a) the maximum speed, b) the number of seconds for which the speed was constant, c) the total distance covered. (ii) State the time-period during which a) the speed was increasing, b) the speed was decreasing, c) the acceleration was zero.
Think first: On a speed–time graph the height is speed and the area underneath is distance — so the whole question is read off one trapezium.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p237-q08 from workbook page 237.

solutionSteps.instruction: Read the greatest height reached by the graph.

contentBlocks.value: The graph levels off at the 12 line

solutionSteps.instruction: Read where the horizontal section starts and ends.

contentBlocks.value: Flat from t = 6 s to t = 10 s, so 10 − 6

solutionSteps.instruction: Identify the shape under the graph.

contentBlocks.value: A trapezium with parallel sides 13 s (whole base) and 4 s (the flat top), and height 12 m/s

solutionSteps.instruction: Match each section of the graph to the description asked for.

contentBlocks.value: Rising line = speeding up, flat line = no change in speed, falling line = slowing down
Result: 0–6 s rising, 6–10 s flat, 10–13 s falling

strategyBlocks.value: Read the maximum height and the flat section straight off the graph, then find the total distance as the area of the trapezium formed by the three straight sections.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) a) 12 m/s  b) 4 seconds  c) 102 m  (ii) a) from 0 s to 6 s  b) from 10 s to 13 s  c) from 6 s to 10 s

whyThisWorks.value: Distance is speed multiplied by time, and on a speed–time graph that product is exactly the area of the strip under the curve — so the whole distance is the area of the trapezium. Acceleration is the gradient of the graph, so a horizontal section means the gradient is zero and the athlete is neither speeding up nor slowing down, even though he is still running at 12 m/s.

commonErrors.misconception: Confusing a speed–time graph with a distance–time graph and reading the flat part as 'at rest' — here the athlete is moving fastest.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Confusing a speed–time graph with a distance–time graph and reading the flat part as 'at rest' — here the athlete is moving fastest.

examTip.value: Write 'area under speed–time graph = distance' beside the graph before you start, and split the shape into a rectangle plus triangles if the trapezium formula feels risky.
